Findings:

- Opening another project first flushes pending changes from the current project.
- That flush calls `git check-ignore -z -- <paths>` to avoid committing files excluded by `.gitignore`.
- Git only permits `-z` with `--stdin`, so the command always fails when paths are supplied as arguments.
- The defect was introduced with the recent project-folder Git exclusion work. Unit tests mocked Git and asserted the invalid command, so they did not detect it.
- The command is unrelated to loading the new project itself. It protects ignored files while saving the old project.

Proposed solution:

Change the ignored-path query to `git check-ignore --stdin -z`, pass NUL-separated paths through stdin, and extend `GitProcess` to support stdin input. Add a real temporary-repository regression test covering ignored and non-ignored paths, plus a project-switch test confirming pending changes flush successfully.

> That flush calls git check-ignore -z -- <paths> to avoid committing files excluded by .gitignore.

what, why?

The app writes pending changes to disk and then commits them. Some project folders may now be configured as local-only through `.gitignore`.

Before running `git add`, `git check-ignore` identifies which changed files must remain local. Those paths are written but not staged; tracked files are still committed normally.

It runs during project switching because the current project’s pending changes must be saved before the app replaces it with the new project. The intent is valid; only the Git command syntax is wrong.
this makes little sense. why are we using git to see this? it is a project configuration setting
I’ll verify how the configuration is represented and why the implementation still consults Git, because your distinction is important.

We currently have the [commit_batcher.ts](app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts), it saves all files and commits them to git.

But, we sometimes don't want to commit the design folder and instead just keep it local. So we should add a configuration option (on project level) that allows the user to turn on/off if the design folder is committed or not.

This option should also be available when opening a project for the first time and we show the dialog for setting up the project folders. By default, the 'include in git' flag should be off, so the design folder should not be committed.

Also, when turned off, we need to add the folder to the git ignore list and remove it when turned on. This can perhaps be a bit of a tricky situation cause we need to make certain git doesn't trip up when we exclude a folder.

## Current state

The configured `projectFolder` is the design folder; it contains active cards, actions, diagrams, releases, and archives. `CommitBatcher` sends every queued project-file change through `StorageService.commit`. Local storage writes each file, stages its path, and commits it. Project setup also commits placeholder files and default actions. No code manages `.gitignore` or supports local-only project files.

`ProjectConfig` has no include-in-Git field. Existing projects therefore always include `projectFolder`. Folder setup collects only folder paths and runs for local and GitHub projects. `md2.config.json` stays at repository root and is committed separately from `projectFolder`.

## Implementation details

- Define â€œdesign folderâ€ as configured repository-relative `projectFolder`. Add project config boolean `includeProjectFolderInGit` under Git settings.
- Existing configs that omit field resolve it to `true`, preserving current behavior. New local-project setup explicitly defaults it to `false`. GitHub and read-only projects always use `true`; do not show or apply option there.
- Add â€œInclude project folder in Gitâ€ control to local folder setup and local project Git settings. Do not allow exclusion when `projectFolder` is empty because repository root cannot be treated as separate local-only folder.
- When local setting is `false`, `CommitBatcher` persistence writes project-folder changes to disk without staging, committing, or pushing them. Setup creates missing folders and default action files locally without attempting `git add` on ignored paths. `md2.config.json` remains committed.

Add normalized root-anchored entry for `projectFolder` inside uniquely labelled MDÂ²-managed block when exclusion is enabled. Preserve every unrelated line, newline style, and existing `.gitignore` file. If file does not exist, create it. Never delete `.gitignore`, including when managed block was its only content.

Confirmation runs `git rm --cached` for folder, updates `.gitignore`, and commits config, ignore rule, and index removals. Cancel keeps previous setting and Git state; unrelated draft config changes may still save.

Cover missing-field migration, local/GitHub visibility, setup defaults, confirmation accept/cancel, tracked-file removal without disk deletion, write-only batching, re-enable behavior, empty and absent `.gitignore`, preservation of unrelated ignore content, and failure handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing project without field opens with â€œInclude project folder in Gitâ€ on and keeps current Git behavior.
- New local project opens folder setup with option off. Confirming setup commits `md2.config.json`, adds project folder to `.gitignore`, and leaves all project-folder files local and untracked.
- GitHub and read-only projects neither expose nor apply local-only option.
- Disabling option for tracked project asks for confirmation before Git-index removal. Accepting removes tracked project-folder paths from index, keeps files on disk, adds ignore entry, and saves disabled value. Cancelling changes none of those items.

- Enabling option removes only managed project-folder ignore entry and saves enabled value. It does not add or commit existing project-folder files.
- `.gitignore` remains present after every enable/disable transition. All unrelated content and formatting remain unchanged.
- Exclusion cannot be enabled when `projectFolder` is repository root.

You are right. The project configuration should be authoritative.

The current implementation unnecessarily uses `.gitignore` as a second runtime source of truth. It asks Git which paths to skip because mixed save batches can contain both local-only project files and committed files. That is an implementation shortcut.

The correct design is:

- Use `includeProjectFolderInGit` and `projectFolder` to split each save batch.
- Write local-only paths without staging them.
- Commit the remaining paths normally.
- Use Git only when changing the setting: update `.gitignore`, check/remove already tracked files, and commit that transition.

`.gitignore` should protect against external Git usage; it should not decide MD² persistence behavior. Therefore, the proposed fix should remove `git check-ignore` from the normal save and project-switch flow, not merely correct its syntax.

Started md2 in debug mode, opened a project automatically, wanted to open another project, got this error:

> Command failed: git check-ignore -z -- design/active/F_5_sphere_defense_cv.md design/usage_metrics.csv
> fatal: -z only makes sense with --stdin

can no longer open another project.

also, what is the purpose of the git command when opening a project?

## Current state

Opening another project first flushes pending changes from the current project. Local persistence calls `listIgnoredPaths`, which runs `git check-ignore -z -- <paths>`. Git only accepts `-z` with `--stdin`, so the flush fails before the new project starts loading.

The ignored-path query was added for the local-only project-folder feature. It runs for normal commits regardless of `includeProjectFolderInGit`, making Git ignore rules a second source of truth for persistence. The project configuration already identifies the local-only folder and must be authoritative. `.gitignore` is only the matching repository safeguard.

The existing tests mock the Git process and assert the invalid arguments, so they do not exercise the real Git command.

## Implementation details

- Remove `listIgnoredPaths` and `git check-ignore` from normal save, move, setup, pending-write, and project-switch persistence paths.
- Partition pending changes using `includeProjectFolderInGit` and `projectFolder`. Write local-only paths to disk without staging, committing, or pushing them. Commit the remaining paths normally, including when one batch contains both kinds.
- Apply the same configuration policy to desktop-generated project files, including activity files and `usage_metrics.csv`, before registering them as uncommitted Git writes.
- Keep Git operations only for changing the setting: maintain the MDÂ² `.gitignore` block, detect tracked project-folder files, and remove confirmed files from the index.
- Replace mocked command assertions with regression coverage using a temporary Git repository. Add focused coverage for mixed batches and switching projects with pending changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- A project with pending changes can open another project without running `git check-ignore` or reporting a Git error.
- With `includeProjectFolderInGit` enabled, pending project-folder changes, activity files, and usage metrics are committed before switching projects.
- With `includeProjectFolderInGit` disabled, project-folder changes are written locally and are not staged, committed, or pushed.
- A mixed batch writes local-only project-folder files and commits only files outside that folder.
- Changing the setting still updates the MDÂ²-managed `.gitignore` block and handles already tracked project-folder files through the existing confirmation flow.
- A real-Git regression test fails with the previous command and passes with the corrected persistence flow.
